title: Does Lifestyle Information Improve Hypertension Prediction? A Leakage-Controlled Evaluation on NHANES
abstract: arXiv:2611.19302v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Does readily available lifestyle information improve machine-learning prediction of hypertension beyond routine demographic and anthropometric data? On NHANES 2017-March 2020, five model families (Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Gradient Boosting, Bagged Decision Trees, and XGBoost) were evaluated with fold-local preprocessing and paired bootstrap confidence intervals. Adding physical activity, alcohol use, smoking, and sleep information showed no consistent detectable improvement in held-out discrimination: every paired ROC-AUC confidence interval included zero, including under a stricter measured-blood-pressure phenotype and without synthetic oversampling. Mean cross-model SHAP rank agreement fell from 0.873 to 0.806 over all encoded columns, but this decline was largely attenuated over the 19 baseline columns shared by both arms (0.873 vs. 0.863), and likewise under both robustness checks; attribution-agreement comparisons across

translated_title: 生活方式信息能否改善高血压预测？基于NHANES的防泄漏控制评估
translated_abstract: 现成可获取的生活方式信息能否在常规人口统计学与人体测量学数据之外，提升机器学习对高血压的预测能力？本研究基于NHANES 2017年至2020年3月的数据，对五种模型家族（逻辑回归、随机森林、梯度提升、装袋决策树和XGBoost）进行了评估，采用折内局部预处理与配对自助法置信区间。结果表明，在加入体力活动、饮酒、吸烟和睡眠信息后，模型在留出集上的判别能力没有一致的可检测提升：所有配对ROC-AUC置信区间均包含零，包括在更严格的实测血压表型定义下以及不使用合成过采样的情况下也是如此。在所有编码特征列上，跨模型SHAP排名平均一致性从0.873下降至0.806，但在两个实验组共有的19个基线列上，这一下降在很大程度上被减弱（0.873对0.863），在两项稳健性检验下同样如此；归因一致性比较……
tldr: 在NHANES数据上经过严格防泄漏控制的评估表明，在常规人口统计与人体测量数据之外加入体力活动、饮酒、吸烟和睡眠等生活方式信息，并不能一致地提升机器学习对高血压的预测性能。
en_tdlr: A leakage-controlled evaluation on NHANES shows that adding readily available lifestyle information (physical activity, alcohol use, smoking, and sleep) does not consistently improve machine-learning hypertension prediction beyond routine demographic and anthropometric data.
